about: Every INCPG independent variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 138 variables INCPG independent writes to CADs/INCPG/incpg_independent_equations_onshape.txt, in that order; 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file (including the small module module_s: the CAD file has one module) and every config key the CAD does not use; 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks INCPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/incpg_independent.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each planet gear is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 (one bearing per gear, half the gap each; mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_s_calc = b1
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule: fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material and the safety factors, so the optimiser has no freedom over it

cad_variables.name: fw_p_b
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each planet gear is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 (one bearing per gear, half the gap each; mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_p_b = b1 (raised)
cad_variables.reason: big-planet face width from the tooth-stress rule, raised to hold its bearing

cad_variables.name: fw_r
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each planet gear is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 (one bearing per gear, half the gap each; mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_r = b2 (raised) + standard_clearance_1_5mm (the CAD's ring width is the stress width plus one standard clearance)
cad_variables.reason: ring face width: the small planet - ring stress width (raised to hold the planet bearing) plus standard_clearance_1_5mm; kept as a stress rule because the shared rule names fw_r that way, and the small planet's width fw_p_s is a copy of it

code_only.name: module_s
code_only.reason: the small module (small planet, ring): searched by the optimiser loop and used by the stress rule and the gearbox constraints, but not in the CAD file, which has one module (same pattern as CPG bug 18)

code_only.name: motor_peak_torque
code_only.reason: motor torque the gears are sized for (peak torque under the default rating setting); sets the face widths

code_only.name: gear_allowable_stress
code_only.reason: allowable tooth stress of the gear material, chosen with the material mode (3dp: PLA, metal: steel); sets the face widths

code_only.name: FOS
code_only.reason: factor of safety in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: serviceFactor
code_only.reason: service factor on the motor torque in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: planet_bearing_gap
code_only.reason: axial gap between the two planet bearings (one in each planet gear); with the bearing width it sets the smallest planet and ring widths

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter
code_only.reason: largest gearbox diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter): the stator's outer diameter times a factor

code_only.name: actuator_width
